- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to anticipate downward pressure.
- Lag in response to recent price drops — model often holds too high a price for 1–2 days after a dip.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp rallies, then underreacts to subsequent pullbacks.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early 2024 (e.g., 2024-02-05) when sentiment is weak and prices are consolidating.
- Sentiment correlation: when sentiment is rising, model forecasts should be slightly higher than historical mean, but not by more than 10–15% above recent 7-day average.
- Avoid “overfitting to recent highs” — if last 3–5 days are high, don’t assume continuation; sentiment must confirm before increasing forecast.
